waiting.title: 42043 Mercedes-Benz Arocs 3245, function 11: the wheels move and the differential's case stays
waiting.what: A change to a function list. Function 11 (the rear axles’ differentials) holds the drive shaft still and turns one wheel of the third axle; its note says the other wheel then turns the opposite way. But the list names the differential’s case (p2036) as the part that moves. With the drive shaft held the case cannot turn: the shaft holds it. The change names the two wheels (p2219, p2227) as the parts that move and the case as the part that stays.

The worker tried it in the viewer (the model lifted, the drive shaft’s universal joint p2029 frozen, the collision pass ready): a turn of one wheel by half a radian turns the other by half a radian the opposite way, and the case stays still.

waiting.title: 42114 6x6 Volvo Articulated Hauler, function 2: the ring extension does not slide when the gearbox shifts
waiting.what: A change to a function list. Function 2 says the L motor shifts the gearbox by turning a catch that slides the driving rings. Its list names the catch, the three rings and also the yellow ring extension (p53) as parts that move. But the extension does not slide: it sits on the axle against its gear, and only the rings slide to it (booklet step 17). The change takes p53 out of the list; the catch and the three rings stay.
waiting.effect: Function 2 goes from partly working to working. The worker checked it on its branch with the whole set; preview keeps the old list and result until you sign.
waiting.confidence: High. The booklet shows the extension put on the axle against the red gear, and Claude ran the L motor in the viewer with the collision pass ready: the catch turns, the three rings slide in turn and come back, the extension stays, and the truck stays where it is.

waiting.title: 42050 Drag Racer, function 4 (the wheelie): the actuator’s input gear drawn off its axis
waiting.what: A correction to the published file. The knob in front of the right rear wheel works a small linear actuator through two bevel gears. In the file the 12-tooth double bevel on the actuator’s input is drawn 0.7 LDU off the actuator’s axis and turned 15.0 degrees where the actuator is at 14.6, so it meshes with nothing and the knob drives nothing. The booklet’s step 64 builds the two bevels meshing at the actuator’s end, on its own axis. The correction puts the double bevel on the axis, turned as the actuator is.
waiting.effect: Function 4 goes from partly working to working: the knob turns the bevels and the actuator’s rod slides. Nothing else in the set changes. A limit you should know: in the viewer the rod slides 0.73 LDU for a quarter turn of its input and the car’s nose does not visibly rise in so short a stroke; the list counts the bevel and the rod, not the nose.
waiting.confidence: High: step 64 shows both bevels and where they sit, and step 69 shows the pair from below. Claude tried it in the viewer with the correction switched on and the collision pass ready: the knob turned 1.5 radians turns the bevel 86 degrees and slides the rod 0.73 LDU, with no stop; the worker saw the same.
